title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers + routing/payload limits for OpenAI compat and tool-calls
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Motivation: Several production incidents and ongoing flaky e2e tests showed the API gateway's streaming proxy and routing code could either drop chunks or incur large tail latency when handling large tool-calling payloads and OpenAI-compatible streaming sessions. This PR applies conservative, backward-compatible tuning to routing rules, per-route payload limits, and the streaming proxy buffer semantics to improve stability and predictable latency while preserving OpenAI compatibility and structured tool/function calling behavior.

Summary of changes:
- Reduce default streaming proxy write buffer flush interval and add adaptive backpressure when downstream is slow.
- Introduce per-route payload soft-limits with configurable truncation/validation hooks to avoid unbounded memory growth in tool-calls.
- Update OpenAI-compatibility layer to preserve chunk boundaries for function_call and structured outputs (fixes broken tool call framing in some proxy cases).
- Add telemetry and tracing points for dropped/chunked frames and per-request routing decisions.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for buffer/backpressure logic
- [x] Integration tests for OpenAI-compatible streaming with function_call flows
- [x] E2E smoke test against dedicated staging cluster
- [x] Docs updated (openai-compat.md + api-gateway tuning guide)

Related: Linear ENG-2148 (streaming stability), ENG-2267 (openai compat tool-calls). See incident SUP-8421 for production traces. This description is intentionally condensed; see commits and changed files for details.

release_notes:
- API Gateway: improved streaming stability by adding adaptive flush/backpressure in the streaming proxy, reducing tail latency for slow downstreams.
- API Gateway: per-route soft payload limits to prevent unbounded memory growth for large tool/function-calling payloads; default 1MB with configurable policies (truncate|reject|warn).
- OpenAI compatibility: fixed chunk boundary preservation for function_call and structured outputs to avoid broken tool-call framing when proxying.
- Observability: added metrics and tracing to monitor buffer flushes, dropped frames, and payload truncations.
notes: Deployed to staging for 48h with no regressions; rollout to prod behind feature-flag and per-route opt-in. Ops runbook updated with alert thresholds for proxy.buffer.dropped_frames.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: changes are opt-in per-route and conservative by default; primary risk is misconfiguring soft-limit policies which would truncate large tool payloads. Operators should audit routes with tool-calls before enabling stricter policies.
